book.answer: Polymarket itself publishes no historical order book. Its /book and /books endpoints return only the current resting book, keyed by token_id alone, with no time parameter. /prices-history returns a single price series ({t, p}); the docs call it an "observed price" and never say whether it is the midpoint or the last trade. The orderbook subgraph stores only fills (OrderFilled and OrdersMatched events), never resting orders. Historical L2 depth exists only in archives that third parties recorded live, and the earliest dates found are Oct 11, 2025 (Telonex, paid), Oct 14, 2025 (Dome), Nov 2025 (PredictionData, paid), Feb 2026 (TickFoundry, paid, and the free PMXT archive, whose downloader starts at 2026-02-21T16:00Z) and Mar 2026 (Marketlens, paid). One vendor, PolymarketData, claims full-ladder 1-minute history "from each market's creation date", but gives no start date and no collection method, so the claim is unverified. Under this task's rules (public sources only: no login, no account, no paid API), the best ask and depth at an arbitrary past second cannot be rebuilt for markets that closed between 2025-01-01 and about 2025-10-10. For later markets they exist only in paid archives. The one free route is PMXT for hours from 2026-02-21 onward, and its host refused or timed out from this machine. The verdict for historical execution in the window 2025-01-01 to 2026-10-31 should therefore be UNVERIFIABLE, except for markets PMXT actually covers once access is confirmed.

book.details:
(1) What Polymarket's own docs and API spec offer:
- /book takes only token_id and returns the resting bids and asks. /books takes up to 500 token_ids and returns the same thing for each.
- Each book response carries a hash and a timestamp. Neither endpoint has any time or as-of parameter, and the docs mention no historical book endpoint anywhere.
- The websocket market channel (book, price_change, last_trade_price, tick_size_change, and best_bid_ask when the extra feature flag is on) is a live feed. The market-stream section mentions no replay.
- /prices-history returns {t, p} points:
  - Old CLOB spec: the interval enum is max/all/1m/1w/1d/6h/1h, and fidelity is "in minutes, default 1".
  - New data-api v2 page: the price is described only as an "Observed price". Retention floors are 1-minute data for at least 7 days, 5-minute for at least 60 days and 30-minute for at least 90 days. Explicit start/end ranges are capped at 15 days.
- Neither the old spec nor the new page says whether p is a midpoint or a last trade. The docs on displayed prices say the UI shows the midpoint, or the last trade when the spread is wider than $0.10.
- /prices-history carries no bid, ask or size data, so it cannot stand in for an ask.

(2) Subgraph:
- The schema of Polymarket/polymarket-subgraph/orderbook-subgraph has these entities: MarketData, OrderFilledEvent, OrdersMatchedEvent, Orderbook (trade and volume counters only) and OrdersMatchedGlobal.
- Its handlers are OrderFilled, OrdersMatched and TokenRegistered.
- It stores fills only, never resting orders. Orders are matched offchain, so unfilled orders never appear onchain.
- Goldsky, Dune and Allium are listed in Polymarket's data-resources page as sources of onchain activity. Allium also has a Beta "market-orderbook" snapshot table, with no start date or access terms stated.

(3) Third-party archives, all recorded live, with the earliest coverage found:

| Source | Earliest coverage | Detail | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| Telonex | Oct 11, 2025 | book_snapshot_5/25/full | paid; 5 trial downloads need an account |
| Dome API | Oct 14, 2025 | orderbook history | not checked |
| PredictionData.dev | Nov 2025 | order books | Pro plan, $400 a month |
| TickFoundry | Feb 2026 | 25-level L2 | paid; free one-day sample of 2026-08-19, BTC 4h series |
| PMXT archive | downloader starts 2026-02-21T16:00Z | free public hourly Parquet; book_snapshot and price_change events | public, but unreachable from here |
| Marketlens | Mar 2026 | L2 about every 60 s plus deltas | paid from $39 a month; the free tier covers only the last 7 days |
| PolyOrderbooks | no start date given | crypto markets only; free Zenodo dataset of 805 resolved crypto markets (CC BY 4.0) | free dataset; live API not checked |
| PolymarketData | claims "from each market's creation date" at 1-minute resolution | no start date, collection method or pricing stated | not stated |

No public Kaggle or Hugging Face dataset was found covering general markets in 2025.

Conclusion for markets that closed between 2025-01-01 and 2026-10-31:
- Before Oct 11, 2025: no verifiable source of the best ask and depth was found. The only claim is PolymarketData's, and it is unverified.
- Oct 2025 to Feb 2026: paid vendors only.
- From Feb 21, 2026: the free PMXT archive, in principle, at event-level fidelity, so the book could be rebuilt to the second for markets it covers. Its coverage per market and the gaps in it were not verified.

Without paid access, historical execution for this study's window should be marked UNVERIFIABLE. Any fill simulation built on /prices-history or on onchain fills is hypothetical, not a verified execution.
book.not_verified:
- archive.pmxt.dev and its docs page were unreachable from here (both WebFetch and curl got connection refused or timed out). PMXT's start date, its free status and its event and snapshot schema therefore come from secondary pages (evan-kolberg.github.io and polymart.app), not from PMXT's own docs. No PMXT file was downloaded or inspected.
- All vendor coverage claims are the vendors' own marketing and were not tested. That covers PolymarketData's "from creation" claim, Telonex, Dome, PredictionData, TickFoundry, Marketlens, PolyOrderbooks and Allium. No account or paid API was used.
- No live call to /prices-history was made. What p means (midpoint or last trade) and how much 1-minute data survives for markets resolved in 2025 were not checked empirically.
- Dune was not checked for any order-book table; only the subgraph schema was read.
- No Kaggle, Hugging Face or Zenodo listing was opened directly. The Zenodo dataset is described only on the PolyOrderbooks page.
- Allium's market-orderbook start date and access terms are unknown.
- Read times are given as a date only (2026-11-17); exact UTC times were not recorded.

fees.answer:
2025-01-01 to 2026-03-29: Polymarket charged no trading fees on politics, geopolitics, culture or business markets. The only fees in early 2026 were taker fees on crypto markets (15-minute markets from 2026-01-05, then all crypto timeframes for markets created after 2026-03-06) and on NCAAB and Serie A sports markets (from 2026-02-18).

From 2026-03-30 ("Fee Structure V2"), taker-only fees apply to Politics, Finance, Tech and Mentions (taker rate 0.04), to Economics, Culture, Weather and Other/General (0.05 after the correction below), and to Crypto (0.072, later 0.07) and Sports. Geopolitics and world-events markets stayed fee-free (rate 0) for the whole period. Makers are never charged. Maker rebates are 25% of taker fees for the non-sports, non-crypto categories, 20% for Crypto, and 15% for Sports from 2026-07-10.

The formula changed once:
- 2026-03-30: `fee = C*p*feeRate*(p*(1-p))^exponent`, where C is the number of shares and p the price. Politics used exponent 1, for a 1.00% peak.
- From 2026-03-31/04-01 (by 2026-04-01 at the latest): `fee = C*feeRate*p*(1-p)`, the exponent field is effectively 1, and fees are charged in shares on buys and in USDC on sells. For politics this means $1.00 per 100 shares at 50c, which is 2% of notional.

Scope over time:
- Docs from 2026-03-30 to 2026-04-14: "Fees apply only to markets deployed on or after the activation date. Pre-existing markets are unaffected."
- By 2026-04-22 that sentence had been replaced with "Fees are determined per-market at match time." The CLOB V2 cutover was 2026-04-28.
- Today, July-2025 politics markets show feesEnabled=true. The date they became fee-bearing could not be verified.

Gas: trades are settled on-chain by Polymarket's operator, and wallet operations through the Relayer are gasless for the user.

Per-fill fee on record:
- Yes, on-chain. CTF Exchange v1 and v2 `OrderFilled` has a `uint256 fee` field, and v2 also emits `FeeCharged(receiver, amount)`.
- No, in the public Data API v2 `Trade` schema (no fee field). Positions have had `entryFeesUsdc` since 2026-08-10.
- The authenticated CLOB get-trades carries `fee_rate_bps`.
- The per-market fee parameters are the Gamma fields `feesEnabled` and `feeSchedule {rate, exponent, takerOnly, rebateRate}`. The legacy `maker_base_fee`/`taker_base_fee` (`makerBaseFee`/`takerBaseFee`) are not the charged fee: politics markets currently show makerBaseFee=1000 although makers are never charged.

fees.details:
Timeline for non-sports, non-crypto-price event markets:

1) 2025-01-01 to 2026-03-29: no trading fees.
- The June 2025 docs snapshot says no fee of any type.
- The 2026-01-22 snapshot says the "vast majority" of markets are fee-free and only 15-minute crypto markets have taker fees.
- The changelog has no 2025 fee entries.
- So any fill in a politics, geopolitics, culture or business market before 2026-03-30 should carry fee 0.

2) Fee rollout on other categories: crypto 15-minute markets from 2026-01-05 (peak 1.56%, crypto rate 0.25 with exponent 2); 5-minute crypto markets launched with fees on 2026-02-12; NCAAB and Serie A sports from 2026-02-18 (rate 0.0175, exponent 1); all crypto timeframes for markets created after 2026-03-06.

3) 2026-03-30, Fee Structure V2. The docs snapshot of 2026-03-30 09:53 UTC gives:
- formula `fee = C*p*feeRate*(p*(1-p))^exponent`;
- Politics 0.04, exponent 1, 25% rebate, 1.00% peak; Finance 0.04 (50% rebate); Culture 0.05; Economics 0.03 (exponent 0.5); Weather 0.025 (exponent 0.5); Other/General 0.2 (exponent 2); Mentions 0.25 (exponent 2); Tech 0.04; Geopolitics 0;
- "Fees apply only to markets deployed on or after the activation date. Pre-existing markets are unaffected."

4) By the 2026-04-01 snapshot, the formula was corrected to `C*feeRate*p*(1-p)`:
- Politics, Finance, Tech and Mentions 0.04; Economics, Culture, Weather and Other 0.05; maker rate 0 everywhere; 25% rebate.
- Secondary reports (KuCoin and Odaily, 2026-04-01, citing Polymarket Discord) say the error used dollar volume instead of shares and added an extra index, which distorted weather and economics markets.
- The "pre-existing unaffected" sentence remained until at least the 2026-04-14 snapshot. It was gone by 2026-04-22, replaced with "Fees are determined per-market at match time".

5) 2026-04-28, CLOB V2 cutover: new exchange contracts, pUSD collateral, and fees set at match time (no `feeRateBps` on orders).

6) Rates for these categories are unchanged from 2026-04-22 through 2026-11-12 in every archived version I checked. The only rate changes in those snapshots are Crypto 0.072 to 0.07, Sports 0.03 to 0.05 (with the rebate cut to 15%) on 2026-07-10, and the new Combos category at 0.05.
- Current page: Politics 0.04, Culture 0.05, Finance 0.04, Economics 0.05, Other 0.05, Tech 0.04, Mentions 0.04, Geopolitics 0. Fees are rounded to 5 decimals with a minimum of 0.00001.
- There is also a taker rebate program (current page, start date not checked).

Fees per fill:
- On-chain: the v1 CTF Exchange `OrderFilled` has a `fee` field. The v1 `CalculatorHelper` computes it from the signed `feeRateBps` as `baseRate*min(p,1-p)*...`, a different shape from the 2026 formula. v2 `OrderFilled` also has `fee`, and v2 emits `FeeCharged(receiver, amount)`.
- APIs: the Data API v2 Trade schema has no fee field (Data API v1 is retired). The authenticated CLOB `/trades` has `fee_rate_bps`. Gamma market objects carry `feesEnabled` and `feeSchedule`.
- The legacy `maker_base_fee`/`taker_base_fee` fields are 0 on a 2021 CLOB market and 1000 on current politics markets. That contradicts "makers are never charged", so they cannot be used as the fee actually paid.

Gas: user wallet operations through the Relayer are gasless, and the operator submits matched trades on-chain.

Implication for the execution study: replays should use `feesEnabled` and `feeSchedule` per market and per date, or the on-chain `OrderFilled.fee`/`FeeCharged` values. They should not assume a blanket category rate, because older markets were declared exempt at least from 2026-03-30 to 2026-04-14.

A link to the 2026-04-28 V2 cutover is plausible but unverified. Settling it needs on-chain `FeeCharged`/`OrderFilled.fee` checks on old markets, which I did not do.
- The exact time on 2026-03-30 when fees went live, and the exact time the formula was corrected (official changelog date 2026-03-31, docs snapshot 2026-04-01). The account of the bug comes from secondary press citing Discord, not from a page I read on Polymarket's own site.
- Whether the Gamma `feesEnabled`/`feeSchedule` fields are versioned over time. They are current snapshots, not history.
- The meaning of the legacy makerBaseFee/takerBaseFee=1000.

- I did not use the 0xinsider, predictionhunt or medium pages.
